text.p: Following is known information compiled from industry sources on scheduled oil refinery maintenance in the Gulf region this year.
Maintenance work at Kuwait's main refinery at Mina al-Ahmadi refinery has been completed on target and will return to full operating capacity on Saturday, industry executives said.
Further work is planned at al-Ahmadi in September and October with a "loss in crude of 115,000-120,000 barrels per day (bpd) for a couple of weeks," a source said.

Work at the Oman Mina-al Fahal refinery was completed in March-April and Oman Refining Company has tendered to buy leaded gasoline for first-half May delivery to replenish stocks that were drawn down during the 30-35 day-long maintenance shutdown.
A vacuum unit at the 250,000 Sitra refinery in Bahrain is scheduled for shutdown in April and a crude unit is planned to be shutdown in June.

Upgrading and expansion work at Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery will not be completed till at least the second quarter of 1998 "and possibly beyond," the Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) newsletter reported this week.
Work at the 265,000 bpd plant had been expected to be completed in the first quarter of next year.

Iran has delivered its first cargo of heavy crude to its new 232,000 bpd refinery at Bandar Abbas this week. An inauguration ceremony for the plant -- the country's eighth major refinery -- is expected in May.
